text:
incident-bot: [ALERT] 03:12 UTC - spike of cuda:IllegalAddress on inference-pool-gpu-2. 14 pods entering CrashLoopBackOff. Auto-escalating to P0.
sara: saw it on the dashboard, spike started ~03:11. pulling logs now.
raj (oncall): I'm on it. tagging @eng-runtime @eng-sre. doing quick triage.
cheng: quick q — any pattern on sequence length or KV cache hits before the errors?
sara: logs show `cudaErrorIllegalAddress` originating from `kv_cache.cpp:312` right after a page-in event. snippet: 
```
[03:11:22] ERR cuda:IllegalAddress at 0x7ff... in load_kv
stack: gpu_kernel+0x1b2
```
dave: customer impact estimate: 3 tenants (=acme-inc, beta-runner, internal-sim) saw ~5-10% request failures with 500s. if we don't contain, risk cascading OOMs on other nodes.
anita: @sara can you confirm exact customers & window? will prep external note if >10% for >15m.
sara: impacted: acme-inc (high QPS test), beta-runner, internal-sim. peak 03:11–03:17. some routes auto-fell back to cpu-variant.
raj (oncall): mitigation plan: 1) cordon affected nodes 2) drain affected pods with `--delete-local-data` 3) scale fallback CPU pool 4) divert traffic for high-risk customers. doing step 1 now.
sara: commands: 
```
kubectl -n inference cordon gpu-node-12
kubectl -n inference drain gpu-node-12 --ignore-daemonsets --delete-local-data
```
dave: throttling batch sizes to reduce KV pressure: set `BATCH_MAX=8` via configmap and rolling update.
cheng: preliminary repro shows misaligned write when allocator returns a chunk without 64B alignment under heavy concurrent frees — plausible allocator/kernel race. would prefer allocator alignment safeguard as hotpatch.
eng-runtime: options: A) set `--disable-persistent-kv` to avoid reuse (slower) B) hotfix allocator. which is faster?
raj (oncall): Option A is lowest-risk to implement fast. flipping flag for affected pods to opt out of persistent KV.
sara: `kubectl -n inference set env deploy/model-server PERSISTENT_KV=false` — rolling restart in progress.
incident-bot: Update: 6 pods restarted, error rate down ~60%.
anita: drafting customer comm: "We experienced transient CUDA errors causing inference failures for a subset of requests. We have applied mitigations and are investigating root cause." will post after review.
maria: collecting core dumps + /var/log/nvidia-persistenced.log + /var/log/kern.log for bug report. uploading to s3://redwood-incident/2062003000.
cheng: need exact backtrace + GPU driver version to escalate to driver/vendor. I'll try a targeted allocator patch and run a canary on a single node.
raj (oncall): handing off to night oncall @lee in 30m. @lee can you take watch after 03:45 UTC? I'll leave runbook notes in pager.
lee: taking handoff at 03:45. I'll keep the cordon in place until patch validated. ping me for any immediate regressions.
eng-sre: recommend we mark as SEV2 now that fallback reduced customer impact but still elevated. scheduling postmortem 10:00 UTC.
anita: posting external status now; cc @support to triage any inbound tickets.
incident-bot: Incident update: severity -> SEV2. last update 03:24 UTC. next update in 30m or on status change.
raj (oncall): summarized action items: collect dumps, run allocator patch canary, confirm driver version, finalize customer note. handing to @lee.
lee: confirmed. monitoring hooks live. will escalate immediately if 500s > 5% for 3m.
cheng: opening PR for allocator alignment safeguard and requesting expedited review from @eng-runtime. will run CI + canary build.
maria: logs & cores uploaded: s3://redwood-incident/2062003000/cores.tar.gz
anita: external status: "Mitigations in place; working on root cause; updates every 2 hours." will update after patch merges.
incident-bot: Monitoring continues; incident remains open for follow-up and postmortem. invites sent for review meeting.
